items.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998
items.q: I watched men like Victor Young, I’ll never forget, we played a main title for Cecil B. DeMille and Victor was a magnificent orchestrator... I was on the date.

ctx.x: What was the repertory at that time. Swing tunes?

Well I don’t think we — only maybe “Honeysuckle Rose” was supposed to swing. “Lady Be Good” I think, that’s about as contemporary as I got you know. And then there were, I’m ashamed to say I don’t remember them now, but there were pop songs so-called. But that’s when I first learned what standards were, you know Victor Young, “Sweet Sue,” songs like that I began to learn. And then I began to learn what time meant, which is my — if you’ve been around my spa here, I collect clocks. I live in a time factory. That…
I guess in an atmosphere like a roadhouse or night club, you learned the importance of playing requests?
